coverageNote: Audited every current Markdown source file in the scoped domain: 9 audit units and 55 files.

findings.claim: An owner is assigned, but no deadline is recorded for deciding whether an accepted offer is legally binding or only an executed contract binds; contract formation cannot be implemented without inventing the binding event.

evidence.excerpt: Is an accepted offer legally binding, or does binding effect begin only when the contract is executed?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether acceptance creates an enforceable agreement before contract execution.
findings.failureScenario: A party treats an accepted offer as cancellable while another treats it as binding, producing an unresolvable cancellation and remedy dispute.

findings.claim: An owner is assigned, but no deadline is recorded for deciding how postponement is represented; booking, hold, contract, schedule, and ticket-manifest behavior cannot be built without inventing whether postponement is a state change or a successor booking.

evidence.excerpt: Postponement is not yet modelled: whether it is a state transition or a new booking affects the hold, contract, schedule, and ticket manifest.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose state-transition versus replacement-booking semantics and which records carry forward.
findings.failureScenario: A postponed show retains its hold or payment schedule in one subsystem but creates a second live obligation in another.

findings.claim: An owner is assigned, but no deadline is recorded for resolving the canonical hold-protocol owner; two units claim the hold ladder, so expiry, conversion, and conflict behavior cannot be implemented without inventing an authority boundary.

evidence.excerpt: 17.01 and 17.02 both claim ownership of the hold protocol. Both cannot own it.
Which unit owns the canonical hold protocol?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the authoritative hold state machine and its owning aggregate.
findings.failureScenario: Offer acceptance and calendar availability apply incompatible expiry or release transitions to the same date.

findings.claim: The announcement gate conflicts on whether deposit receipt is waivable: confirmation treats it as waivable while deposit collection makes it an enforceability condition, so publication logic has no single contract.

evidence.excerpt: P-07 Deposit received is a Tier 2 prerequisite and may be waived.
Does the waiver model conflict with the requirement that deposit receipt gates announcement?
The deposit gate before announcement determines whether the booking is commercially enforceable.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose whether an authorized waiver permits announcement before the deposit is received.
findings.failureScenario: A show is publicly announced under a waiver, then downstream enforcement rejects it as unconfirmed.

evidence.excerpt: Does publishing avails require book or list?

findings.forcedInvention: Choose the authorization claim required to publish availability.
findings.failureScenario: A user with only one of the two claims can either publish improperly or is blocked from a valid workflow.

findings.claim: Parallel offers sharing a bill or budget are explicitly out of scope even though two live threads for one date are routine, so acceptance cannot atomically protect shared capacity.

Shared state is not modelled: a sibling acceptance can exhaust budget that another thread assumes remains available.

findings.forcedInvention: Choose locking, reservation, and rollback semantics for shared bill, date, and budget capacity.
findings.failureScenario: Two negotiators accept compatible-looking offers concurrently and overcommit the same talent budget or bill slot.
